stem.en: Waves are cutting a cave into a headland. Which is the right match of process and job?

text.en: Hydraulic action: moving water loosens rock. Abrasion: carried rock grinds it.

feedback.en: Yes. One is the force of the water, and the other is grinding by what the water carries.

text.en: Abrasion: moving water loosens rock. Hydraulic action: carried rock grinds it.

feedback.en: No. The names are swapped. Hydraulic action is the force of moving water.

text.en: Both of them: the sea drops its sand, and the sand hardens into new rock.

feedback.en: No. Dropping sand builds. Neither of these processes builds anything.

text.en: Both of them: wind blows dry salt into the rock over many thousands of years.

feedback.en: No. Both are the work of moving water, not wind.

explanation.en: Hydraulic action is erosion by the force of moving water, which loosens and removes material. Abrasion is the grinding of the rock by the sand and stones the waves carry.

hints.en: "Hydraulic" has to do with water. The other one works by rubbing.
